featured_techniques.technique: Humility and remorse as a corrective approach
Humble Pie branding to accompany apology
Communicate the solution widely and emphasize values

sections.description: Opening remarks on the importance of humility and remorse, with a reference to a home health care case (Nurse Next Door) as an example.
sections.title: Intro: humility and remorse; Nurse Next Door reference

sections.description: Describes that a mistake should be followed by a substantial apology and a branded, tangible remedy (the Humble Pie Company) as part of accountability.
sections.title: Humble Pie analogy and apology

sections.description: Notes the financials: $1,500 spent on pies, with $150,000 saved in business after solving the problem.
sections.title: Cost and impact of the remedy

sections.description: Advocates communicating the solution to everyone, including those unaware of the problem, because values are demonstrated during service recovery.
sections.title: Marketing the solution; values on stage

summary: This short talk frames humility as a practical response to service mistakes. It cites a real-world case (Nurse Next Door) and a fictional partnership with the Acme Humble Pie Company to illustrate not only a sincere apology but also a tangible remedy. The speaker emphasizes that a modest financial investment (spending on humble pies) can yield a large return by repairing trust, and that the remedy should be communicated broadly to reinforce the company’s values on display during recovery.
title: Humility in Action: Apology, Remedy, and Marketing the Fix
